summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever and neutropenia eight days after high-dose Cytoxan for stem cell mobilization in the setting of multiple myeloma. He presented with somnolence, attributed to recent narcotic and Xanax use, and was found to have very low white blood cell and platelet counts. He was treated with IV cefepime, later broadened to vancomycin due to persistent fevers, though all cultures remained negative. Imaging showed mild bronchiolitis, likely viral, and no bacterial source was identified. His neutrophil count gradually recovered, fevers resolved, and IV antibiotics were discontinued in favor of oral levofloxacin. A tunneled pheresis catheter was placed on discharge day, and his first stem cell collection was successfully completed. He was discharged home in stable, afebrile condition to continue daily pheresis sessions and oral antibiotic therapy.
